solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Opposition of English female I encountered during social occasion

indicators.note: met in the middle of something, so the letters sit inside the occasion word

parts.note: a dance is a social event

explanation.surface: Someone recalls meeting resistance from an Englishwoman at a party.
explanation.definitionFit: Opposition and resistance to authority are synonyms, as in standing in open challenge.

clue.text: End of day or start of day over river

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits above the second
the opening letter of the word day is taken

parts.note: the Usk is a river in Wales

explanation.surface: A choice of whether the river scene is set at evening or at dawn.
explanation.definitionFit: Evening twilight comes as daylight ends, so it is the close of the day.

clue.text: Strong point favouring team — first half

parts.note: to be for something is to favour it

indicators.note: only the opening two of the four letters of team are kept

explanation.surface: A pundit notes that the side's strength showed in the first half of the match.
explanation.definitionFit: A forte is a speciality or strength, borrowed from French for strong.

clue.text: Got hold of suitable crossword finally

parts.note: appropriate means fitting or suitable

indicators.note: the closing letter of the word crossword is taken

explanation.surface: Someone at last laid hands on a crossword that suited them.
explanation.definitionFit: To appropriate something is to take it for oneself, to seize possession of it.

clue.text: Fold your attire finally into case

indicators.note: the picked letters are put inside the word case
the closing letters of the words your and attire are taken

explanation.surface: Advice to fold your clothes at last and pack them into a suitcase.
explanation.definitionFit: A crease is the line left where cloth or paper has been folded.

clue.text: Hints about what someone showing contempt might do

definitions.text: what someone showing contempt might do

indicators.note: turned about, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: tips are hints or pieces of advice

explanation.surface: Clues are offered as to how a scornful person might behave.
explanation.definitionFit: Expelling saliva at or near someone is a traditional gesture of scorn.

clue.text: Tradesman, quietly, to move awkwardly

parts.note: P is piano, the musical direction for quietly
to lumber is to move heavily and clumsily

explanation.surface: A workman is pictured shuffling around clumsily and quietly.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who fits and repairs water pipes is a skilled tradesman.

clue.text: Tied up Edward around that place

indicators.note: the name goes around the other piece, enclosing it

parts.note: Ted is a short form of Edward
there means in that place

explanation.surface: Edward has been bound up somewhere over there.
explanation.definitionFit: An animal on a rope fastened to a post is tied up and kept from straying.

clue.text: Complete hour to reconstruct temperature-sensing device

indicators.note: to rebuild something, so these letters are put together in a new order

explanation.surface: Instructions to rebuild a full hour, as if time itself could be reassembled.
explanation.definitionFit: This instrument joins two different metals and reads heat from the small voltage produced.

clue.text: End with Romeo in fit of temper

indicators.note: the letter goes in among the letters of the other word

parts.note: to stop is to end
R is Romeo in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Romeo's story ends with him in a rage.
explanation.definitionFit: A strop is informal British slang for a sulk or tantrum.

clue.text: Run out of Gold Street going after former husband

indicators.note: the gold and street pieces follow the first pair of pieces

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife
H is the abbreviation for husband in genealogy
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: Someone has run out of money on Gold Street, chasing an ex-husband.
explanation.definitionFit: To exhaust a supply is to use it up completely.

clue.text: Older batsmen needing replaced: that can be shown

indicators.note: placed again in a different order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cricket selector says veteran batters must be dropped, and the case is provable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needing' is a link word. In cricket, a batsman is a player whose job is to bat.
explanation.definitionFit: Something demonstrable is capable of being proved or clearly displayed.

clue.text: Tom cries uncontrollably — it's cold and windy

indicators.note: out of control, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Tom is sobbing helplessly because the weather is bitter and blustery.
explanation.definitionFit: A winter storm bringing freezing rain is cold, and storms are windy.

clue.text: Fruit in cold fortified wine — no starter!

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

indicators.note: the wine loses its opening letter

parts.note: sherry is a fortified wine from Spain

explanation.surface: A fruit served chilled in sherry, with no first course before it.
explanation.definitionFit: A small round stone fruit, red or black, grown on trees of the genus Prunus.

clue.text: Circle round the globe

parts.note: the imaginary line drawn around the middle of the Earth, equidistant from both poles

explanation.definitionFit: The great latitude line at zero degrees encircles the Earth halfway between the poles.

clue.text: What sounds like vulgar series of lectures maybe

indicators.note: the answer is said the same as a word meaning vulgar

parts.note: coarse means crude or vulgar

explanation.surface: A query about what crude-sounding lectures might be.
explanation.definitionFit: A university module, a set of classes on a subject, is an example of this; 'maybe' signals it.

clue.text: Letter from apostle's so righteous

indicators.note: the letters are taken from within the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: An epistle written by a virtuous apostle, like Paul's letters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Letter' looks like an epistle, but here it means one who lets property out.
explanation.definitionFit: A landlord who lets out property under a lease is one who lets.

clue.text: Food items with unusual gloss, as a rule

indicators.note: not in the usual form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Snacks that, as a general rule, have an unusual shine.
explanation.walkthrough: A sausage roll is a British snack of sausage meat baked in pastry.
explanation.definitionFit: These pastry snacks are a kind of food, often eaten at parties.

clue.text: Promise not to use top shelf

indicators.note: in a down clue the top is the first letter, which is dropped

parts.note: a pledge is a promise

explanation.surface: A vow not to use the top shelf.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrow flat projection, as from a wall or cliff, is a kind of shelf.

clue.text: Leader sobs when upset

indicators.note: upset means knocked over or disturbed, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A leader breaks down crying when distressed.
explanation.definitionFit: A head of an organisation, the person in charge, is its chief.

clue.text: Vents in shops?

definitions.meaning: openings through which air, water or steam escapes
retail stores selling a maker's goods, marked by the query as a looser sense

explanation.definitionFit: Pipes releasing gas are openings for escape, and stores are points of sale for products.

clue.text: Professional brings in editor: a Spaniard?

indicators.note: the first piece takes the second inside it

parts.note: pro is short for professional

explanation.surface: A professional hires an editor, who might be from Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: Pedro is a common Spanish man's name, so its bearer is perhaps from Spain; the query marks an example.

clue.text: Difficult situation of maiden facing anger

indicators.note: the first piece stands in front of the second, facing it

parts.note: M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over
ire is anger

explanation.surface: A young woman in a tough spot confronts someone's rage.
explanation.definitionFit: Being stuck in a bog is the literal sense; figuratively, a predicament or mess.

clue.text: Terrible regrets about English welcoming people

indicators.note: the shuffled letters go around the single letter
terribly wrong, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Awful remorse surrounds the English way of welcoming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Terrible' rearranges REGRETS as GRE TERS, split around E.
explanation.definitionFit: Staff who meet and welcome visitors at a door are hosts receiving guests.
